contacts.name: Chandrasekhar Panda
contacts.comment:
Persuasion

is important in a project proposal because you’re hoping your audience will read your proposal and do something for you in return. If your reader isn’t intrigued by your project, they won’t feel inclined to help you. If you describe your editing tool but don’t mention the many features it will offer, how it will benefit clients, and its positive impact in the industry, your audience will wonder, “Why should I care about this project?”

contacts.name: Chungulu Chunga
contacts.comment: Be sure to add aria-expanded to the control element. This attribute explicitly conveys the current state of the collapsible element tied to the control to screen readers and similar assistive technologies. If the collapsible element is closed by default, the attribute on the control element should have a value of aria-expanded="false". If you’ve set the collapsible element to be open by default using the show class, set aria-expanded="true" on the control instead. The plugin will automatically toggle this attribute on the control based on whether or not the collapsible element has been opened or closed (via JavaScript, or because the user triggered another control element also tied to the same collapsible element). If the control element’s HTML element is not a button (e.g., an <a> or <div>), the attribute role="button" should be added to the element.

qna.question: Are these my own articles?
qna.answer: Most of the articles are just some brief with a link to the real article, there is a section called Originals, which are my own articles

qna.question: Which areas do you cover?
qna.answer: I want to cover areas such as Science, Technology, Psychology, Medicine and Art, but I have options for contributors to contribute to any area they want.

qna.question: What is the motive behind "Article Collection" ?
qna.answer: My motive is to present a ad and clutter free reading experience, I starting this as as my own collection of articles and plan to expand to bigger knowledge base.

qna.question: Server Version?
qna.answer: Java based server with Spring Boot, H2 database and React front end, I plan to add more features in future.

qna.question: How are the articles picked?
qna.answer: Each category has a hand-picked list of reputable sources, such as journals, magazines, museums and space agencies. A collector reads new articles from those sites, checks each site's robots.txt first and keeps its requests slow and polite. Sites that ask not to be read are skipped.

qna.question: Do you copy the whole article?
qna.answer: No. For each article I keep only the title, author, publish date, a short summary and the main image, with a link back to the original. The full piece is always on the original site, and the author and source are credited on every article.

qna.question: Which categories can I browse?
qna.answer: Art, Engineering, History, Mathematics, Medicine, Philosophy, Physics, Psychology, Science, Software Development, Space and Technology. Pick a category on the Home page to see everything in it, or choose All to see the latest from every category.

qna.question: How often are new articles added?
qna.answer: New articles are collected in batches. Each batch is reviewed before it's published, so there's no fixed schedule, but the collection keeps growing. Links that have appeared before are skipped, so the same story never shows up twice.

qna.question: Are there ads or paywalls?
qna.answer: There are no ads and nothing to pay for here, and you don't need an account. Some of the original sources may have their own paywalls or sign-up prompts when you follow a link to read the full article.

qna.question: Do you track what I read?
qna.answer: Only in a simple way. When you open an article, the site records a view: which article it was, the time, your IP address and an approximate location (country and city) looked up from that address. I use this to see which topics people read. There are no cookies, no ad trackers and no third-party analytics.

qna.question: What happens to the details I send through the Contact page?
qna.answer: Your name, email, optional phone number and message are saved so I can read and reply to them. They aren't published on the site or shared with anyone.

qna.question: Can I suggest an article or a source?
qna.answer: Yes, please do. Send it through the Contact page with a link and a line on why it's worth reading. The same goes for broken links or mistakes you spot in an article.

qna.question: Can I print an article?
qna.answer: Yes. Use your browser's Print option, and the page prints just the article without the menu and footer. Printing this Q&A page includes every answer, even the closed ones.

qna.question: What is this site built with?
qna.answer: It runs on zJournal, a small self-hostable journal app I built with React and TypeScript. The same site can run on a Node, PHP, Java or Python server, and the server in use is listed under "Server Version?" above.
